label: copy-phase input k (fed-back k) at later recall positions
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, almost exclusively (99.2% of activation mass) when the input is the token k, i.e. the model has just emitted and fed back a k that was original token recall_idx-1. Never fires in the original phase, on the delimiter, or on the first occurrence of k. Magnitude grows with how late in the copy the k is: weak or absent when k is fed back at recall_idx 1-2 (k at original positions 0-1), strong (near max) at recall_idx >= 4, and firing rate also rises with t and as to_go shrinks. Residual misses are faint activations (<0.1 of max) on non-k copy-phase inputs near the end of long sequences. False positives are mostly fed-back k at recall_idx 3 with many outputs still to go in long sequences.

issues: Most factual claims hold on dev. Activity is 100% copy phase, with none in the original phase, on <DEL>, or when in_first==1. in_tok==k carries 99.2% of the mass. recall_idx 0-1 never fire, and recall_idx 2 fires weakly (precision 0.17, mass 1.8%). The rate rises with t and as to_go shrinks. Non-k firings are faint and scattered (precision 0.003, mass 0.8%; restricting to to_go<=1 & L>=7 or seen(k) still gives precision about 0.01).

There is a systematic false-positive class. A fixed recall_idx >= 3 cutoff is wrong because the onset depends on sequence length. In copy, recall_idx + to_go = L-1, so the feature's gating is a function of position relative to L. The original predicate's false positives on test (4950) are mostly k fed back at recall_idx 3 (step 10-12) in L=7-9 sequences. The explanation names this class but treats it as noise.

A length-relative cutoff, (phase==2)&(in_tok==k)&(3*recall_idx >= L+2) (equivalent to 2*recall_idx - to_go >= 3), raises test precision from 0.914 to 0.979. Test recall goes from 0.836 to 0.854, F1 from 0.873 to 0.912, and mass recall from 0.973 to 0.988. False positives fall from 4950 to 1135. Dev F1 is 0.912 vs 0.874.

The explanation says swapping in a to_go cutoff scored lower. That is true for a to_go-only cutoff. But combining recall_idx with to_go (equivalently, recall_idx relative to L) beats both, so the claim that recall_idx >= 3 is the best gating is wrong.
The label 'at later recall positions' is roughly right but vague. Lateness is relative to L (roughly the last two-thirds of the copy), not an absolute index of 3 or more.
skeptic.revised_label: fed-back k in the copy phase, past roughly the first third of the copy (onset scales with sequence length)
